subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or rely on narrower per-job/message-delivery safeguards?
rationale: The issue is not a narrow bug fix because it chooses a new public config surface and security precedence model for automated runs.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and tests for fresh and existing cron jobs.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as policy-equivalent to subagents where safe, reducing new config surface but coupling two session classes.

options.title: Keep per-job safeguards only
options.body: Avoid a new global config surface and address duplicate message delivery or tool exposure through narrower cron-run guards.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and tests for fresh and existing cron jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron runtime work and prior review context make this the best available owner for the policy direction choice.
